title: Dependency Releases on Disability Compensation Awards with Individual Unemployability: Months Priced from the 100 Percent Tier
content:
**Rule.** The months of a Disability Compensation dependency release priced from the 100 percent tier are:

- **every month it covers**, when individual unemployability is granted and the whole months from individual unemployability's effective date to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment, less one for each monthly payment that came back, are at least the months covered;
- **that many months alone**, the others priced from the award's own tier, when individual unemployability is granted and they are fewer;
- **none**, every month priced from the award's own tier, when the decision history shows no individual unemployability granted.

Individual unemployability's effective date is the effective date on the most recent rating decision granting individual unemployability. The count of months from it never falls below nothing.

**100 percent tier amounts** (each month so priced): spouse addition 220.30; spouse aid-and-attendance addition 201.41; child addition 146.10; school-child addition 472.95; parent addition 176.88.

**Worked case (hypothetical award at Disability Compensation (70% Combined Rating), one spouse on the claims, release covering 6 months).** Individual unemployability is effective 20 November 2025, the most recent monthly payment was issued on 1 April 2026 and no payment came back: 4 whole months, fewer than 6. Four months are priced at 220.30 and two at the 70 percent tier's 154.21: 881.20 plus 308.42, that is 1189.62.

| Individual unemployability | Its months against the months covered | Months at the 100 percent tier |
|---|---|---|
| Granted | 7 against 6 | 6 |
| Granted | 6 against 6 | 6 |
| Granted | 4 against 6 | 4 |
| Not granted | — | 0 |
